segments.content:
Chapter 110: 0107 Starting a Business is Hard Work

The internal testing period for Xiaoneiwang was tentatively set for two months.

The first month would mainly be used to find bugs, verify the stability of the core modules, debug browser compatibility, and so on.

In the second month, invitation codes would be gradually increased to let users invite their own friends, allowing them to observe the speed of natural viral growth and user retention rate data. At the same time, they would test server stability with 500 to 1,000 concurrent users.

The specific timeline could be adjusted slightly.

Once they confirmed that the core process had no fatal flaws, user retention exceeded 50%, and the number of new daily users reached a certain level, they could move from internal testing to open beta ahead of schedule.

In the middle to late stages of internal testing, they also needed to complete a server expansion and build an initial customer service system to handle the influx of a larger user base during the open beta phase.

Chen Guiliang carefully sorted through it all.

The server was temporarily borrowed from Peking University, but it had to be returned when the time was up, and they would need to expand further if user numbers grew. A sum of money had to be prepared for that.

One part-time customer service representative would be enough for now. If there were too many users and they couldn't handle it, they could hire a full-time one later. That meant an increase of one to two customer service staff.

Two development and maintenance personnel were enough for the time being, namely Guo Feng and a part-time programmer. If they got too busy, they would hire another full-time programmer. That meant an increase of one programmer.

As for the product manager, Chen Guiliang would take on the role himself.

Senior Sister Ao could lead part-time students in ground promotion. Ao Yanchan had been quite effective at promoting Sanguosha at Tsinghua, and she was very capable, so she could be brought onto the team.

Dong Qianqiu and another part-time programmer were responsible for developing the online version of Sanguosha. They would need to hire more staff later on, and the voice acting for the game would also cost money.

After moving into the new office building, they would need at least some basic renovations and to purchase various office supplies.

Money was a bit tight.

"How much do you plan to borrow?" Wang Kai asked.

Chen Guiliang asked in return, "Teacher Wang, how much can I borrow in my situation?"

Wang Kai didn't answer directly, but instead began to explain in detail, "There are three types of loans."

"First, I can help you contact the Zhongguancun Science Park. Using your Sanguosha and Xiaoneiwang as collateral, you can borrow 40 to 60 percent of your projects' valuation. But neither of your projects is fully established yet, so I think it will be very difficult to pass the loan assessment."

"Second, loans from the municipal and district governments. The former requires you to hire a sufficient number of employees with Beijing household registration, and the latter requires you to have been established for over six months and meet a revenue threshold. You don't meet either requirement."

Chen Guiliang thought to himself: Since I can't get either of these loans, what's the point of you even mentioning them? To show off your own importance?

Wang Kai continued, "The third type is from our park's incubation fund, which invests in the form of debt or convertible bonds. Do you know what debt and convertible bonds are?"

"I do. They're just professional terms for borrowing money," Chen Guiliang asked, "What's the interest rate?"

Wang Kai said, "Low interest, with an annual rate of 0 to 4 percent. The exact rate depends on your project's value. The central bank's current benchmark lending rate is 5.58 percent. Additionally, you're allowed to only repay the interest for the first two years."

Chen Guiliang said sincerely, "Those are very generous terms."

Wang Kai smiled, "A startup like yours can only borrow between 50,000 and 500,000 yuan. I'll see what I can do and try to apply for as much as possible for you. But I suggest you hold off on borrowing for now and wait until after Xiaoneiwang's open beta. If the website's data is promising, I can get you the full 500,000 yuan and even push for a lower interest rate."

"Thank you, Teacher Wang." Chen Guiliang was in high spirits.

At the same time, he carefully recalled all his past interactions with Wang Kai, trying to figure out if Wang Kai had hinted at anything.

It seemed like he hadn't implied anything.

Better not to offer a gift rashly, lest it backfire. He could invite him to a meal next time, at a slightly higher-end restaurant, and see if he agreed.

Chen Guiliang left the incubation office, then stopped at the door. "Teacher Wang, when will the science park building's basic interior renovations be finished?"

"It's already done and currently under inspection. I'll notify you as soon as you can officially move in," Wang Kai said.

Chen Guiliang thanked him again, went downstairs, hopped on his bicycle, and whistled as he rode back to the university for class.

The building completed this year was called the Peking University Science Park Innovation Center, also known as the Peking University Science Park Tower.

It had 16 floors above ground and 3 floors below.

Peking University had also built Changchun New Garden as a supporting facility, which had both student dormitories and talent apartments for the science park. In the future, Chen Guiliang's company employees could live in those apartments.

"The sparrows outside the window, chattering on the telephone pole..."

Chen Guiliang was in such a good mood that his whistling gradually turned into singing.

His bicycle entered through the East Gate of Peking University and headed straight for the Second Classroom Building.

The class he was about to attend was "Introduction to Logic," taught by a Professor Liu who had graduated from Peking University's Department of Mathematics.

Thankfully, it was just an introductory course, and his middle and high school math knowledge was sufficient. Otherwise, Chen Guiliang would have had a really hard time.

When he arrived at the classroom, it was still early, and only half the seats were taken.

"CEO Chen, gracing us with your presence in class?"

Just as Chen Guiliang sat down, a freshman from the Department of Philosophy joked with him.

"If I don't show up again, I'm afraid I'll fail the course," Chen Guiliang sighed. "I didn't listen at all last class. When I was trying to self-study with the book, all those symbols made my head spin."

Another student asked, "CEO Chen, when is Xiaoneiwang going to add the invite-a-friend feature?"

"Did you register an account last night?" Chen Guiliang asked.

The student smiled, "CEO Chen personally invited me, so I definitely had to show my support. The features on your Xiaoneiwang are so much better than the alumni websites. It's definitely going to be a hit once registration opens to the public."

"I'll take that as a good omen. Let's go binge out at the South Gate sometime." Chen Guiliang had actually already forgotten this person's name.

He had made too many friends to remember them all.

Several other students put their books on desks to save their seats and came over specifically to chat with Chen Guiliang.

Some asked about Sanguosha, some about Xiaoneiwang, and some discussed writing poetry.

This scene completely baffled the students who were not in the know.

"Who's that guy? He seems really popular."

"Don't know him."

"I know him. He's Chen Guiliang, a freshman from the Yuanpei Program. The guy started doing business right after school started, launched two companies at once."

"For real?"

"Why would I lie to you?"

"Must be a rich kid, right? His family must be loaded."

"He's from the countryside. He rode a beat-up bicycle everywhere to promote Sanguosha. I heard the money he used to start his companies came from fees he earned writing articles."

"That's just too awesome!"

Chen Guiliang's fame was growing bit by bit.

Of course, some people were disdainful and would sneer at the mention of his name.

After listening attentively through the entire class, Chen Guiliang was back on his bike, rushing off again.

A very busy man.

It was exhausting!

Outside a small recording studio, the reporter Lai Dandan had already been waiting for over ten minutes.

"What took you so long?" Lai Dandan complained.

Chen Guiliang quickly explained, "I rushed over as soon as class ended."

Lai Dandan said, "You really are busy."

Peking University's Department of Art Studies had small recording studios, and they could also get students from the musicology program to do voice acting cameos.

The main reason was the price was cheap; it could be settled with a barbecue meal.

Recording here for an hour only cost 80 yuan. If they went to the recording studios around Zhongguancun, like Zhongke Recording Studio or Red Lantern Recording Studio, the hourly rate was three to five hundred.

Actually, Peking University's radio and television stations could also be used for recording, and for free, but the sound quality was too poor. The procedures were also quite troublesome, requiring an application to the University Youth League Committee or the Propaganda Department.

Lai Dandan led Chen Guiliang inside. "Let me introduce you. This is Kong Yuke from the musicology program, and this is..."

"Hello, Senior Brother Kong. Sorry to trouble you."

"Hello, Senior Sister Wang..."

They were all amateurs.

They majored in music history, music theory, music composition... there was even a course called "Music Psychology."

They were quite skilled at analyzing or composing music, but their voice acting was probably not even as good as Bian Guanyue's.

But it was good enough to use. The main selling point was that it was cheap.

When he had money in the future, he would re-record the voices for Sanguosha and get Bian Guanyue to voice Zhen Ji.

"Father, big brother, I, Zhongmou, have let you down!" Senior Brother Kong began to voice Sun Quan.

After one take, Chen Guiliang said, "Senior Brother Kong, Sun Quan isn't from the Northeast. Please mind your accent and try not to let your dialect slip out."

Senior Brother Kong said, puzzled, "I ain't speaking no Northeastern dialect."

"Alright, let's keep recording. Senior Brother, just try to rein it in a bit." Chen Guiliang almost wanted to do it himself.

With a makeshift team, they could make do with anything.

Lai Dandan stood to the side, stifling a laugh. She was the one who had helped introduce all these senior brothers and sisters.

Senior Brother Kong usually sang very professionally, so how did his voice acting come out with such a strong Dongbei accent?

But a Sun Quan with a Northeastern accent was indeed quite amusing.

Lai Dandan had already sent her interview article about Chen Guiliang to the school newspaper editor, but it hadn't been published yet.

Most students couldn't be bothered to read the school newspaper; they would rather spend that time browsing posts on the BBS.

But about 10 to 15 percent of students would read it, mostly members of the student union and club leaders, as well as others who needed to get information from the university administration.

Occasionally, an issue or two would see a huge surge in readership because the paper had a scholars' column that regularly featured interviews with famous professors, like Mr. Ji, Mr. Li, and so on.

"You guys carry on recording, I have another interview to get to." Lai Dandan watched for a while and then left.

"Take care, Senior Sister."

Since Chen Guiliang wasn't picky about the quality, the voice acting, of varying levels of skill, was finished in just over an hour.

Chen Guiliang and the four amateur voice actors descended upon a barbecue stand at the South Gate. This was the "salary" he paid his senior brothers and sisters.

Right, no money needed.

On the way, he also made a trip to the science park to deliver the recorded voice lines to Dong Qianqiu.

Half-drunk from the barbecue, Chen Guiliang pushed his bicycle back and locked it in front of Dormitory Building 36.

He suddenly didn't feel like going back to his room and plopped down under the pagoda tree in front of the building.

The leaves of the ginkgo trees on the north side of the dormitory were already beginning to fall.

At the hot water building in the distance, male and female students carrying thermoses were queuing up to get water, laughing and chatting about all sorts of interesting things.

At the telephone booth outside the building, a female student lingered for a long time, letting out a few soft laughs from time to time, probably on a 201 phone card talking to her boyfriend from another university.

A few boys walked together to the small convenience store, one of them asking, "Do you sell Sanguosha here?"

The surroundings were bustling and lively, but Chen Guiliang, under the pagoda tree, felt as if he were separate from the outside world.

They are so simple and happy. Is there any point in me working this hard?

Forget it, I'll just go back and get some sleep.

The truth was, Chen Guiliang just had too much on his mind every day. He was enrolled in 14 courses, running two companies, and had to find time to write "Those Things About the Ming Dynasty."

He never had a moment's rest from dawn till dusk, and he was somewhat drained, both mentally and physically.

He finally understood why many student entrepreneurs would suddenly take a leave of absence or drop out while still in school.

The average person really couldn't handle it.

He had to take it easy this weekend, or he was going to burn out. He would go to CUEB to hang out with Bian Guanyue for a day.

(End of Chapter)
